chunks: 3 - He said: Abul Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubair reported to me, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Amr narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:

Al-Harith al-Hamdani called upon the Commander of the Faithful ['Ali ibn Abi Talib], peace be upon him, with a company of the Shi'ah, and I was among them. Al-Harith walked with a bent stature, hitting the ground with his walking stick, and he was ill. So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, turned toward him - and al-Harith had a good standing in his estimation - and said: "How do you find yourself, O Harith?" He replied: "The vicissitude of time has overtaken me, O Commander of the Faithful, and the dispute of your companions at your door has added to my anguish and burning anger. There are extremists who have gone too far among them, and moderates who follow, and waverers who doubt, not knowing whether to advance or recoil." He said: "Suffice it for you, O brother of Hamdan! Be it known that the best of my followers are the people on the middle path. To them the extremist should return, and with them the hesitant should join." Then al-Harith said to him: "If only you would remove - may my father and mother be your ransom - the filth from our hearts, and make us see our affair with clarity."

He (peace be upon him) said: "That is enough for you, for you are a person upon whom confusion is cast. Surely, the religion of Allah is not known by the people, but rather by the sign of the Truth. So know the Truth, and you shall know its people. O Harith, surely the Truth is the best narration, and whosoever proclaims it is a fighter for it. By the Truth I inform you, so lend me your ear, then inform about it whoever among your friends has sound judgement. Be it known that I am a slave of Allah, the brother of His messenger, and his first confirmer - I confirmed him while Adam was between the spirit and the body. Then I am indeed his first confirmer among your nation, truly. So we are the first and we are the last, and we are his special ones, O Harith, and his sincere ones. And I am his cousin, his successor, his trustee, and the possessor of his confidence and his secret. I have been given the understanding of the Book, sound judgement and speech, and the knowledge of the generations and relations. I am entrusted with a thousand keys, each key opens a thousand chapters, each chapter leads to a million covenants. And I am supported and especially chosen and helped by the Night of Qadr as a special gift. And surely that continues for me and for those who guard from among my descendants, for as long as the night and the day pass, until Allah inherits the earth and all who are upon it. And I give you glad tidings, O Harith, you shall recognize me at the time of death, and at the Bridge, and at the Pool, and at the time of Division.

Al-Harith said: "O my master, what is the Division?" He said: "The division of the hellfire. I will divide it with a correct division, saying: This is my friend, so leave him; and this is my enemy, so take him." Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, took al-Harith by the hand and said: "O Harith, I have taken your hand just as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, took my hand and said to me - when I had complained to him of the envy of Quraish and the hypocrites toward me - 'Surely, on the Day of Resurrection, I shall hold the rope of Allah and cling to His safeguard - meaning His protection - from the Lord of the Throne, the Most High, and you, O 'Ali, shall hold fast to my safeguard, and your descendants shall hold your safeguard, and your Shi'ah shall hold fast to the safeguard of all of you. So what will Allah do with His Prophet? And what will the Prophet do with his successor?' Take this, O Harith, the summary from the lengthy. Yes, you are with the one you love, and for you is what you have earned." He said this three times. Then al-Harith stood up, pulling his cloak behind him, saying: "After this, I care not when I meet death or it meets me."

Jamil ibn Salih said: And Abu Hashim al-Sayyid al-Himyari, may Allah have mercy on him, recited to me regarding what this report contains: "The statement of 'Ali to Harith is marvelous / And how many marvels did he carry with him! / O Harith of Hamdan, whoever dies shall see me / Be he a believer or a hypocrite, face to face. / His eyes shall recognize me and I will know him / By his attributes, his name, and by his deeds. / And you, at the Bridge, shall recognize me / So do not fear a stumble nor a slip. / I shall quench your thirst with cool water upon thirst / The sweetness of which you will think is like honey. / I shall say to the hellfire when it is stopped for display / Leave him, do not come near the man. / Leave him, do not approach him, for indeed / He has a rope bound with the rope of the Successor, connected."

key_terms.النَّمَطُ الْأَوْسَطُ: The middle path, the balanced approach among followers, avoiding both extremism and hesitancy
key_terms.الْمُقَاسَمَةُ: The division at hellfire, where Ali separates his friends from his enemies
key_terms.حُجْزَةٌ: Safeguard or protection, used metaphorically for the chain of intercession from Allah through the Prophet to Ali to his progeny to the Shi'ah
key_terms.صِدِّيقُهُ: The truthful confirmer, a title indicating the first and foremost believer in the Prophet's mission
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Decree, an annually recurring blessing given to the Prophet's household

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali tell al-Harith al-Hamdani about the middle path, divine knowledge, and intercession on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah narrates a pivotal encounter between al-Harith al-Hamdani and Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS). Al-Harith, who was ill and distressed by the factional disputes among the Imam's companions, visited the Imam seeking clarity. Imam Ali counseled him that the best of his followers were the moderate middle group, not the extremists or the hesitant doubters. When al-Harith pressed for deeper insight, the Imam declared his unique station: he was Allah's servant, the brother and first confirmer of the Prophet (even before Adam's creation), the custodian of divine knowledge through a thousand keys each opening vast realms of wisdom, and the recipient of the ongoing blessing of Laylat al-Qadr. The Imam gave al-Harith glad tidings of recognition at the time of death, at the Bridge (Sirat), at the Pool (Hawd), and at the Division of hellfire. He then relayed the Prophet's own words about the chain of intercession: the Prophet holding Allah's rope, Ali holding the Prophet's, their progeny holding Ali's, and the Shi'ah holding the family's. Al-Harith departed in joy, declaring he no longer feared death. The hadith concludes with al-Sayyid al-Himyari's poem versifying these themes.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubair reported to me from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahdi, who reported from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn Amru who reported from his father, from Jamil ibn Swaleh, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:

Al-Harith Al-Hamadani called upon Amirul Mu’mineen (‘Ali Ibn Abi Talib) with a company of the Shi’ahs, and I was among them. Al-Harith walked with a bent stature, hitting his walking stick hard on the ground. He was indeed ill. So Amirul Mu’mineen came close to him and al-Harith had a good standing in his estimation, and he said: "How do you find yourself, O Harith?" He said: "The vicissitude of time has overtaken me, and the dispute among your companions about you and the three before you, has added to my anguish and anger. There are those who have gone to the extreme in their passionate love for you, and those who are yours in moderation, and those who waver in doubt, not knowing whether to proceed or recoil." He (‘Ali) said: "Suffice it for you, Oh brother (from) Hamadan! Be it known that my best followers are the people united on the middle path. To them should the extremists return, and with them should the hesitants join." Then al-Harith said: "My father and mother be your ransom, could you (further clarify so as to) remove the filth from our hearts, and (to) make us as sure about our affair as seeing with one’s eyes?"

He (peace be upon him) said: "That is enough for you. You are possessed by confusion. Surely, the religion of Allah is not known (or judged) by the people, it is recognized by the sign of Truth. Know the Truth, and you shall know its people. O Harith, surely Truth is the best (and most sublime) narration, and whosoever utters it is indeed a fighter (a soldier of Truth). I have informed you the Truth, so lend me your ear and inform among your friends who have sound judgement. Be it known that I am a slave of Allah, the brother of His messenger and his first confirmer. I confirmed his truth when Adam lay between the spirit and the body. Then, I am his first confirmer truth among you people. We are the first and we are the last. And we are his special ones with distinction, and we are his sincere ones. And I am his cousin, and his successor, and his trustee and possessor of his confidence and secret. I have been given the understanding of the Book, and (blessed with) sound judgement and decision, and the knowledge about the generations and the relations. And I am entrusted with a thousand keys, each key opens a thousand chapters, each chapter breaks into a thousand testament. And in addition, I am supported and especially chosen and helped by the Night of Qadr, and that continues for me and my descendants who guard against sins, for as long as the days and the nights subsist, till such time when Allah shall inherit the earth and all who are upon it. I give you glad tidings, O Harith, you shall recognize me at the time of death, and at the Bridge, and at the Pool, and at the time of division."

Al-Harith said: "O my master, what is the time of division?" He said: "Division at the hell-fire, when I will make a correct separation. I shall say: This is my friend, so leave him; this is my adversary, so take him" Then Amirul Mu’mineen took (al-Harith) by his hand and said: "I hold your hand the way the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny), held my hand and said (when I complained to him about the envious Quraish and the hypocrites) ’Surely, on the Day of Judgement, I shall hold the rope of Allah and cling to His safeguard, and you, O ‘Ali, shall hold fast to my safeguard, and your descendants shall cling to your safeguard, and your Shi’ahs shall hold fast to the safeguard of all of you.’ So what will Allah do to His Prophet? And what will the Prophet do to his successor? (The same shall we do to our followers). Take this, O Harith, the summary of all the details. Yes, you shall be with the one you love, and for you shall be what you have earned." He said this three times. Then al-Harith stood up, pulling his cloak behind him, and saying: "After this, I care not when Death meets me or I meet it."

Jameel B. Swaleh says that Abu Harith Seyyid al-Himyari, may Allah bless him with mercy, narrated this for me in the following poem: "The statement of ‘Ali to Harith is marvelous, And how much of marvels did he carry with him? (He said) O Harith of Hamadan, whoever dies shall see me, Be he a believer or a hypocrite, a clear sight before him. His eyes shall recognize me, and I will know him, By his attributes, his name, and by his deeds. I shall quench his thirst with cold water, The sweetness of which will seem to you like that of honey. And when you will stand before hell fire, I shall say, Leave him, and do not be near him, Leave him, and be away from him, for indeed, He has a rope bound with the rope of the Prophet’s successor."
